item.title: Four North Carolina homes repaired after Helene face demolition after FEMA buyouts
item.description: In the aftermath of Hurricane Helene, four homes in the Cottages at Cypress Run neighborhood in Hendersonville face demolition due to severe flooding. Previously, these homes were repaired through homeowner efforts and community volunteerism. To address the persistent flood threats, homeowners have chosen FEMA's voluntary buyouts, aligning with the Hazard Mitigation Grant Program's initiative to convert affected land into green spaces, thereby reducing future flood risks. Fuente: The Times of India - World.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Queensland dairy farmer opened four campsites after drought forced her family to sell 40 cows
item.description: Agritourism is gaining momentum among Australian farmers struggling with drought-related financial pressures. Landowners like Libby Rough are transforming their properties into camping havens, creating alternative income streams. This shift not only aids in sustaining their farms during tough times but also promotes local agricultural education among visitors. Moreover, local authorities are streamlining regulations to encourage this thriving sector, enhancing community engagement with farming practices. Fuente: The Times of India - World.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: When the atmosphere slows the Earth: Uncovering a subtle signal of climate change
item.description: Atmospheric circulation governs weather and climate, but it also carries angular momentum. When winds shift or mass redistributes, the atmosphere can exchange momentum with the solid Earth, slightly altering the planet's rotation rate. This is not a new concept, but what happens under long-term global warming? Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Georgia begins 10-year forest restoration at 132-acre Towaliga Preserve with data-centre partnership
item.description: The Towaliga Preserve is about to launch an ambitious 10-year forest restoration project, backed by QTS Data Centres. This significant initiative aims to revitalize 132 acres, focusing on ecosystem management and biodiversity enhancement. Throughout the decade, contractors will engage in tasks like invasive species control and planting native trees. After the project, the Southern Conservation Trust will ensure the area remains cared for and healthy. Fuente: The Times of India - World.
item.dc:creator: TOI Science Desk

item.title: En 1974, Francia necesitaba evitar que París volviera a inundarse. La solución fue tan sencilla como radical: borrar tres pueblos del mapa
item.description: La gran inundación de París de 1910 dejó una imagen difícil de olvidar: calles convertidas en canales, vecinos desplazándose en barca y el Sena alcanzando 8,62 metros en el puente de Austerlitz. Francia necesitaba impedir que una crecida semejante volviera a golpear la capital y terminó adoptando una solución a una escala gigantesca. A unos 190 kilómetros de París construyó un depósito capaz de almacenar 350 millones de metros cúbicos de agua. El problema era que en el lugar elegido ya había algo: bosques, campos y tres pueblos enteros. Algo donde guardar agua. El problema no era únicamente… Fuente: Xataka.
item.dc:creator: Miguel Jorge

item.title: 57 new deep-sea species discovered in Argentina’s Mar del Plata Canyon, including ‘Loki’ sea cucumber
item.description: In a groundbreaking deep-sea voyage off Argentina, scientists uncovered 57 brand new marine species alongside five previously unclassified genera. Using a remotely operated vehicle, they pulled samples from the Mar del Plata Submarine Canyon. Among these marine marvels was a unique and translucent sea cucumber whimsically dubbed Loki. A subsequent collaborative workshop was instrumental in accelerating the species identification process, highlighting the astonishing biodiversity of the South Atlantic's deep ecosystems. Fuente: The Times of India - World.

item.title: A Moroccan mine built a road from phosphate waste rock; field tests cut dust emissions by 91%
item.description: In Morocco, a phosphate mine has implemented an innovative road surface made from waste rock generated during phosphate extraction. This robust, three-layered pavement design not only successfully supports heavy mining vehicles but also helps manage dust emissions effectively. Testing resulted in a notable decrease in airborne dust and enhanced road quality, with an anticipated 15 percent boost in productivity for mining operations, while also cutting down maintenance expenses. item.title: The expansion of Heathrow would be an expensive disaster for Britain and the world. Burnham needs to block it | George Monbiot
item.description: A third runway would fly in the face of reason. If we are to prioritise human life over short-term ‘growth’, we need to use planes less, not more If a third runway is built at Heathrow, what will be the impact on the wealth of the nation? It will cost us somewhere between £23.4bn and £62.5bn. These are not my figures ; they weren’t calculated by environmental groups, but by the Department for Transport. For decades, government ministers have told us that airport expansion is essential for “growth”. As chancellor, Rachel Reeves claimed that a third runway at Heathrow would add 0.43% to GDP… Fuente: The Guardian - Environment.
